It is outside both the weekday conditional (shabbat=false, קֶרֶן בְּמָשְׁכָם) and the marked Shabbat conditional (shabbat=true, instruction אם שבת, קֶרֶן בְּזָכְרָם). The structure therefore keeps it when shabbat is true, false or undecided. This matches JLPTEI-3: a description that covers both readings and the shared words after them (הַיּוֹם עָדֶיךָ…) does not belong inside either branch. The selector run you reported fits this XML. I did not re-run it.

R2 resolved. The second j:option in Misod reads פני <tei:choice><tei:abbr>ממ״ה</tei:abbr><tei:expan>מלך מלכי המלכים</tei:expan></tei:choice> מלא רחמים. That is a nested abbr/expan, not silently expanded text. JLPTEI-3 says readings.abbreviations picks abbr or expan without touching the j:option choice, so the default build shows the printed ממ״ה.

R3 resolved. Each of the three standOff notes has a target that matches an existing tei:choice xml:id exactly: #musaf_uppad_lindan_variant, #musaf_misod_address_variant and #musaf_shofarot_command_variant. The notes are type="commentary" in tei:standOff[@type=notes], which is out-of-line paratext and not recited. In each case the first j:option is the main reading: לִנְדָן, the full פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ…הָאֲדוֹנִים wording, and כְּמִצְוָה.
